content_html:
<p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5"># 狗狗營養缺乏症完整指南 — 症狀識別與補充方法</p><h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-near-black mt-10 mb-3">前言：為何自煮鮮食容易出現營養失衡？</h2><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">很多狗主人都會為毛孩親手準備鮮食，覺得這樣既健康又安心。但你知道嗎？自製鮮食其實暗藏營養陷阱！根據研究，<strong>高達九成自製狗糧都存在營養不均的問題</strong>，尤其是一些關鍵維生素和礦物質的缺乏。</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">這不是要嚇唬你，而是想提醒你：了解營養缺乏的症狀和正確的補充方法，才能讓你的愛犬真正食得健康。</p>

title_en: The Complete Guide to Nutritional Deficiencies in Dogs — Symptoms and How to Fix Them
desc_en: Up to 90% of homemade dog food is nutritionally unbalanced. A vet-style breakdown of the key deficiencies, the symptoms to watch for, and the right way to supplement them.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Most homemade dog diets are missing one or more key nutrients. Knowing which deficiencies show up as which symptoms is the difference between guessing and actually fixing the problem.

Why is homemade food so easy to get wrong?

Plenty of owners cook for their dogs because it feels healthier and safer than kibble. That's a fair instinct. But research puts the share of nutritionally unbalanced homemade dog diets at around 90% — almost always because the recipe skips one or more of the micronutrients dogs can't live without: key vitamins and minerals.

The point isn't to scare you off home cooking. It's to give you a working vocabulary: what deficiency looks like, which nutrients are most often missing, and how to fill the gaps without overdoing it.

content_html:
<p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5"># 狗狗家居按摩治療基礎 — 放鬆肌肉與促進血液循環</p><h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-near-black mt-10 mb-3">為什麼你的狗狗需要按摩？</h2><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">你有冇試過放工返到屋企，成身攰到想攤喺梳化唔郁？其實你嘅狗狗都一樣會有身體疲勞同肌肉繃緊嘅時候。不過佢哋唔識得用說話話俾我哋知，只係會用行為表達——例如唔願郁、行路姿勢奇怪、或者成日舔某個部位。</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">近年獸醫學發展得好快，狗狗嘅壽命比20年前長咗足足兩倍。但壽命長咗，伴隨而嚟嘅就係各種老年病——心衰竭、腎衰竭、關節炎、糖尿病……呢啲慢性病好多時西醫都只能控制，而唔係根治。加上手術同藥物嘅副作用，令愈來愈多主人開始為毛孩尋找更溫和嘅輔助療法。</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">寵物按摩就係其中一種。佢唔係要取代正規獸醫治療，而係作為一種<strong>補充療法</strong>，幫助狗狗放鬆肌肉、促進血液循環、增強免疫力，同時仲可以增進你同狗狗之間嘅感情。</p><h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-near-black mt-10 mb-3">按摩對狗狗嘅12大好處</h2><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">我哋先講啲實際嘅好處，等你明白點解要學呢門手藝：</p><div class="overflow-x-auto my-3"><table class="w-full text-sm border-collapse"><tr><th class="border border-gray-100 px-3 py-2.5 bg-brand-light text-brand font-semibold text-left">好處</th><th class="border border-gray-100 px-3 py-2.5 bg-brand-light text-brand font-semibold text-left">具體效果</th><th class="border border-gray-100 px-3 py-2.5 bg-brand-light text-brand font-semibold text-left">點樣幫到狗狗</th></tr><tr></tr></table></div>

title_en: Home Massage Therapy for Dogs — Relaxing Muscles and Boosting Circulation
desc_en: Canine massage works alongside vet care to ease muscle tension, improve circulation, and strengthen the bond with your dog. Here's how to do it safely at home.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Dogs carry muscle tension and fatigue just like we do — they just can't tell us in words. A few minutes of massage a day relaxes tight muscles, improves circulation, and quietly strengthens the bond between you.

Why does your dog actually need massage?

You've had those days — finish work, get home, every muscle is screaming for the sofa. Your dog has them too. They just can't say it. Instead you see it in their behaviour: reluctance to move, an odd gait, or constant licking at one spot.

Veterinary medicine has come a long way. Dogs today live roughly twice as long as they did 20 years ago. Longer life means more chronic conditions to manage — heart failure, kidney failure, arthritis, diabetes. Western medicine can often control these but rarely cure them, and surgery plus medication come with side effects. That's why more owners are looking for gentler supportive therapies alongside the vet's plan.

Canine massage is one of them. It isn't meant to replace vet treatment. It's a complementary therapy that helps relax tight muscles, promote blood flow, support the immune system, and — as a bonus — deepen the bond between you and your dog.

content_html:
<p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5"># 狗狗鮮食營養指南 — 自煮鮮食的營養比例與食材選擇</p><h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-near-black mt-10 mb-3">前言：為什麼要為狗狗自煮鮮食？</h2><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">香港的寵物主人愈來愈重視毛孩的飲食健康，自煮鮮食已成為不少狗主的新選擇。然而，很多主人在開始自煮鮮食時，最常遇到的問題是：「究竟要落幾多肉？」、「點樣先算均衡？」、「狗狗食鮮食會唔會唔夠營養？」</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">其實，為狗狗準備鮮食，不單是將肉類和蔬菜隨便煮熟那麼簡單。一餐均衡的鮮食，需要考慮蛋白質、脂肪、碳水化合物、維生素和礦物質的適當比例。更重要的是，每隻狗狗的體質都不同，有些狗狗怕冷，有些容易皮膚敏感，有些腸胃較弱——這些都需要透過飲食來調整。</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">這篇文章會從現代營養學和中醫食療兩個角度，教你如何為狗狗設計均衡的鮮食餐單，讓毛孩食得健康又開心。</p>

title_en: The Dog Fresh-Food Nutrition Guide — Ratios, Ingredients, and a Balanced Plate
desc_en: Homemade dog food needs the right balance of protein, fat, carbs, vitamins, and minerals — not just cooked meat and veg. A practical guide for HK owners.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Cooking for your dog isn't just meat plus vegetables. A balanced fresh meal needs the right ratio of protein, fat, carbs, vitamins, and minerals — and that ratio shifts with your dog's body type and condition.

Why cook fresh food for your dog?

Hong Kong owners are paying closer attention to what goes into the bowl, and homemade fresh food has become a real alternative to commercial kibble. The questions that come up the moment you start are always the same: how much meat? How do I know it's balanced? Will my dog miss something by not eating kibble?

Cooking fresh food isn't just a matter of boiling some meat and veg together. A balanced meal needs the right ratio of protein, fat, carbohydrate, vitamins, and minerals. On top of that, every dog is different — some run cold, some have sensitive skin, some have a delicate stomach. Diet should respond to all of that.

This guide walks through both modern nutrition and traditional Chinese food therapy, so you can build a fresh-food menu that keeps your dog healthy and happy at the bowl.

<p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5"># 狗隻中醫五元素養生法 — 體質辨識與食療調理</p><h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-near-black mt-10 mb-3">前言：為什麼要從中醫角度照顧狗狗？</h2><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">你有冇試過，狗狗明明食足三餐、營養均衡，但依然皮毛乾燥、精神不振、成日病？或者，你已經好努力跟足網上食譜整鮮食，但狗狗嘅身體狀況始終冇乜改善？</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">其實，問題可能唔係「食得唔夠」，而係「食得唔啱體質」。</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">中醫養生嘅核心，係講求「整體平衡」。人同狗一樣，身體狀況會隨季節、年齡、情緒同飲食而變化。今日，我哋就用一個全新角度——<strong>中醫五元素（五行）養生法</strong>，幫你了解狗狗嘅體質，再透過日常飲食，由內到外調理好佢哋嘅身體。</p>

title_en: The Five Elements (Wu Xing) Approach to Canine Wellness — Body Type and Food Therapy
desc_en: TCM Five Elements is a framework for reading your dog's body type and tuning the diet to it. A practical primer on Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water dogs.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Some dogs eat well and stay dull and itchy. The Five Elements framework reads your dog as a body type — Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, or Water — and lets you tune the diet and lifestyle to the type, not just to the ingredient list.

Why take a TCM angle on dog care?

Have you ever had a dog who eats three proper meals a day, gets a balanced diet, and still looks dull-coated, low-energy, and constantly a bit under the weather? Or you've followed a fresh-food recipe to the letter and your dog just… doesn't really improve.

Most of the time the problem isn't "not enough food" — it's "not the right food for this particular dog."

Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) thinks in terms of whole-body balance. Dogs and humans are alike in this: body condition shifts with season, age, mood, and diet. Today we're going to use one framework — the Five Elements (Wu Xing) — to read your dog's body type and then dial in the everyday diet to support them from the inside out.

title: 狗隻營養標準比較：AAFCO、NRC 同實際應用
title_en: Comparing the Major Dog Nutrition Standards — AAFCO, NRC, and What Actually Matters for Fresh Food
source: AAFCO / NRC 官方文件＋一手獸醫營養來源
source_en: AAFCO and NRC official documents + primary veterinary nutrition sources
disclaimer: 本文為一般教育資訊，並非獸醫營養處方。設計餐單前請諮詢獸醫營養師。
disclaimer_en: General educational information only — not a veterinary nutrition prescription. Consult a board-certified veterinary nutritionist before changing diets.
desc_en: AAFCO, NRC and WSAVA explained: how 'complete and balanced' is actually defined, why per-1000-kcal and dry-matter comparisons disagree, and the nutrients homemade dog diets most often miss.
content_html:
大部分主人問「我隻狗食得夠唔夠營養」，其實問錯咗問題。真正的問題係：你用邊個標準去判斷「夠」？市面上有三套常用標準——AAFCO、NRC 同 WSAVA 指引——它們解決的問題完全唔同。搞清它們的角色，你才會知幾時可以信一個食譜，幾時一定要找獸醫營養師。

AAFCO 同 NRC：一個管法規，一個講科學

兩個名經常一齊出現，但性質差好遠。

  • AAFCO（Association of American Feed Control Officials，美國飼料管理官方協會）由美國各州飼料管理官員組成。它本身唔係監管機構、無執法權，出的是「模範法規」（model regulation）。各州把它的條文寫入自己的飼料法例之後，才有法律效力。
  • NRC（National Research Council，美國國家科學院體系）2006 年的《Nutrient Requirements of Dogs and Cats》係一份科學評估：用實驗數據推算每種營養素的最低需求（MR）、適當攝取量（AI）、建議攝取量（RA）同安全上限（SUL）。它唔係法規，係科研共識。
  • 一句記法：NRC 答「狗的身體需要幾多」，AAFCO 答「一包糧要符合咩門檻，才可以在標籤上寫 complete and balanced」。AAFCO 的數值部分高於 NRC 的 MR、部分低於 NRC 的 RA，因為它要考慮商業加工損耗與可行性，兩套數字唔可以直接互相替換。

所以「符合 NRC」同「符合 AAFCO」係兩件唔同的事。學術研究常同時對兩邊比對，然後分開報結果；你見到「不達標」三個字，要問清楚係對邊個標準不達標。

「Complete and balanced」在法律上點定義

這句話唔係形容詞，係一個有特定寫法的法律聲明。AAFCO 模範法規規定，寵物食品包裝上要有「AAFCO statement」，只有幾種認可句式：

  • Formulated to meet the nutritional levels established by the AAFCO Dog Food Nutrient Profiles for [生命階段]——即配方計算上達到 profile，唔需要做餵食試驗。
  • Animal feeding tests using AAFCO procedures substantiate that [產品] provides complete and balanced nutrition for [生命階段]——即做過 AAFCO 協議的餵食試驗（成犬維持通常 26 週、成長期 10 週）。
  • Product family member——同系列中一款做過試驗，其他成員按配方相似性沿用結論。
  • Intended for intermittent or supplemental feeding only——即「唔完整」，只可以當零食或配糧。呢句係最重要的反面訊號。

聲明裡面一定要寫清楚物種同生命階段。呢點係消費者唯一可以在包裝上查證的營養聲明，其他 marketing 字眼（天然、人食級、獸醫推薦）在法律上唔等於營養完整。

香港情境：香港冇本地寵物食品營養標準，規管主要靠《商品說明條例》（第 362 章）處理虛假或誤導陳述。換句話講，你在香港買到的糧，標籤上的 complete and balanced 絕大多數係参照 AAFCO（美國）或 FEDIAF（歐洲）的標準寫，本地冇人幫你驗。自己識睇聲明，比信包裝設計實際。

生命階段：growth、adult maintenance 同 all life stages

同一個品牌，同一個配方名，可能分幾個生命階段版本。門檻差別好大：

  • Growth / reproduction（成長與繁殖）：門檻最高。幼犬、懷孕與哺乳犬需要更高的蛋白質、鈣、磷、維他命 D 同能量密度，因為骨骼與組織正在快速建成。
  • Adult maintenance（成犬維持）：門檻最低，只維持體重與日常運作。
  • All life stages（全生命階段）：同時符合 growth/reproduction 與 adult 兩套 profile，實際運作上等於用最高（growth）門檻去做。對一隻絕育成犬來講，長期食 all life stages 通常唔會有害，但能量與部分礦物質會有餘裕，要盯住體重與體態評分。

最常見又最貴的錯誤：幼犬（尤其大型犬幼犬）長期食只標 adult maintenance 的糧。鈣磷比例與絕對量不足，影響的是骨骼發育，好多時幾個月後才看得出來，到時候已經係結構性問題。

點比較數字：每 1000 kcal 基準 vs 乾物質基準

呢個係整篇文章最實用的技術點。罐頭與鮮食含水 75–80%，乾糧約 10%。所以標籤上「蛋白質 10%」同乾糧「蛋白質 26%」，唔可以直接比——前者大部分是水。

  • 乾物質基準（DM basis）：把水分扣掉，用百分比除以（1 − 水分百分比）。用途係比較「濃度」。AAFCO profile 有乾物質欄位。
  • 每 1000 kcal 代謝能（per 1000 kcal ME）：比較「狗實際按能量比例食落肚的量」。AAFCO profile 的主欄位就是這個。為什麼用能量做分母？因為狗是按能量需求進食，唔是按食物重量。一隻 5 公斤犬一日食三百幾 kcal，一隻 30 公斤犬食過千 kcal；同一個百分比，兩隻狗實際攝取的絕對量差幾倍。
  • 實務陷阱：鮮食譜通常寫「每公斤食物」或「每份」，唔會講能量密度。要真正核對，必須用營養計算軟件或成分資料庫（例如 USDA FoodData Central）算出總熱量，再換算成每 1000 kcal 的含量，才有得同 profile 比。

蛋白質與氨基酸：最低百分比唔等於足夠

AAFCO 對成犬的粗蛋白最低要求大約在 18% 乾物質，成長期約 22.5%。呢兩個數字只保證「總量」，唔保證「品質」。

  • 狗需要約十種必需氨基酸（精氨酸、組氨酸、異亮氨酸、亮氨酸、賴氨酸、蛋氨酸、苯丙氨酸、蘇氨酸、色氨酸、纈氨酸），成長期另有牛磺酸相關考量。
  • AAFCO profile 除了粗蛋白百分比，仲有逐項氨基酸最低值。所以「蛋白質 30% 就一定夠」係錯的推論：如果主要蛋白來源是皮、筋、蹄這類膠原含量高的部位，氨基酸剖面可以好差，總量高但質素低。
  • 加工與生物可用率：同一份蛋白質，煮熟與生食、不同動物來源，氨基酸的可吸收比例差別明顯。profile 數字係門檻，唔係品質評分。

自煮鮮食最常缺嘅營養素

最有力的一手數據来自 Stockman 等人 2013 年發表在《JAVMA》的研究：200 個成犬自煮維持食譜，95% 至少有一種必需營養素不達 NRC 或 AAFCO 標準，83.5% 有多重缺乏，只有 9 個食譜符合 AAFCO。四份由獸醫營養專科醫生撰寫的食譜全部達標——呢個對比本身就係結論。

  • 鋅：69% 食譜不足，係最常見缺口。肉類的鋅吸收受植酸、鈣、銅影響，雞胸加白飯的組合幾乎必缺。
  • 膽鹼：64.5% 不足。蛋黃與肝臟含量高，純瘦肉配方容易不夠。
  • 銅：54% 不足。
  • EPA + DHA：53.5% 不足。要來自魚油或脂肪魚；亞麻籽的 ALA 在狗身上轉化率很低，唔可以當等價替代。
  • 鈣：35% 不足；但更危險的是鈣磷比失衡——純肉配方磷高鈣低，對幼犬骨骼發育的影響係即時性的。
  • 反方向亦有風險：該研究有食譜超出維他命 D 與 EPA/DHA 的安全上限；長期大量餵肝臟會造成維他命 A 過量。自煮鮮食的問題唔止「唔夠」，仲有「過多」。
  • 香港情境：高溫高濕，鮮食煮好後室溫放置的時間要短，分裝後冷藏幾日內用完、長期保存靠冷凍。潮濕環境容易黴變與脂肪氧化，會令本來算得準的營養素再打折。所以「計得準」同「存得對」係同一件事的兩半。

用 AAFCO profile 檢查一個食譜的流程，同幾時一定要找獸醫營養師

  • 第一步：定能量。用體重與活動量估算每日熱量需求（獸醫營養常用的 RER／MER 公式），得出每日 kcal。冇能量基準，之後所有比較都做唔到。
  • 第二步：入軟件。把食譜每樣食材的重量輸入營養計算軟件或成分資料庫，得出總熱量與各營養素總量。手算幾個大項（鈣、磷、鋅、熱量）可以，全面核對唔現實。
  • 第三步：換算成每 1000 kcal。逐項對 AAFCO adult maintenance 欄位的最低值，同時要對最高值——超上限同樣係不達標。
  • 第四步：再對乾物質濃度。確認唔係被水分稀釋出來的假達標，也不是濃縮造成的假超標。
  • 第五步：問 profile 答唔到的三個問題。氨基酸剖面（唔止總蛋白）、脂肪酸比例、各礦物質來源的生物可用率。呢三樣係軟件最容易出錯、亦最影響實際結果的地方。
  • 第六步：長期監察。體態評分、體重、毛髮與皮膚、糞便質地、每年血液檢查。食譜一改（換肉類、換補充品品牌）就要重算，唔可以當一次計完就永久有效。

以下情況唔建議自己試：幼犬與大型犬成長期、懷孕與哺乳、任何慢性病（腎、心、胰、泌尿道結石、皮膚或腸道過敏）、長期以自煮為主食、生肉餵食、以及你打算照網上食譜做主食。這些情況要找 board-certified 的獸醫營養師（DACVIM 或 DECVCN 認證），唔係一般獸醫或寵物店員。付一次咨詢費，換的是幾年的骨骼、腎臟與心臟健康，係整個自煮鮮食流程入面回報最高的一筆支出。

參考文獻

  • AAFCO. AAFCO Official Publication（每年更新，含 Dog and Cat Food Nutrient Profiles 及 Model Regulations 章節）。Association of American Feed Control Officials.
  • AAFCO. AAFCO Methods for Substantiating Nutritional Adequacy of Dog and Cat Foods（含餵食試驗協議）。
  • National Research Council. Nutrient Requirements of Dogs and Cats. Washington, DC: National Academies Press; 2006.
  • WSAVA Global Nutrition Committee. Global Nutrition Guidelines 及 Guidelines on Selecting Pet Foods（持續更新）。World Small Animal Veterinary Association.
  • Freeman LM, Becvarova I, Cave N, et al. WSAVA Nutritional Assessment Guidelines. Journal of Small Animal Practice. 2011;52(7):385–396.
  • Stockman J, Fascetti AJ, Kass PH, Larsen JA. Evaluation of recipes of home-prepared maintenance diets for dogs. Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association. 2013;242(11):1500–1505.
  • FEDIAF. Nutritional Guidelines for Complete and Complementary Pet Food for Cats and Dogs（歐洲對應標準，每年更新）。
content_html_en:
Most owners asking "is my dog getting enough nutrition?" are asking the wrong question. The real question is: which standard are you measuring against? Three references dominate the conversation — AAFCO, NRC, and the WSAVA guidelines — and they answer completely different questions. Get their roles straight and you will know when a recipe can be trusted and when you need a veterinary nutritionist.

AAFCO and NRC: one writes rules, one does the science

The two names appear together so often that they get treated as interchangeable. They are not.

  • AAFCO (Association of American Feed Control Officials) is a body of US state feed-control officials. It is not a regulator and has no enforcement power; what it publishes is a model regulation. It only becomes law once individual states adopt it into their feed statutes.
  • NRC (National Research Council, part of the US National Academies) published Nutrient Requirements of Dogs and Cats in 2006. That is a scientific assessment: experimental data used to estimate minimum requirements (MR), adequate intake (AI), recommended allowances (RA), and safe upper limits (SUL) for each nutrient. It is not law — it is scientific consensus.
  • The short version: NRC answers "what does the dog's body need?" AAFCO answers "what threshold must a product clear before it may print complete and balanced on the bag?" Some AAFCO values sit above the NRC MR, others below the NRC RA, because AAFCO also accounts for processing losses and commercial feasibility. The two sets are not swappable.

So "meets NRC" and "meets AAFCO" describe different things. Studies typically compare against both and report them separately. When you read "deficient", always ask: deficient against which standard?

How "complete and balanced" is legally defined

The phrase is not marketing language — it is a legal statement with required wording. Under the AAFCO model regulations, a pet food label must carry an AAFCO statement, and only a few forms are recognised:

  • Formulated to meet the nutritional levels established by the AAFCO Dog Food Nutrient Profiles for [life stage] — the recipe calculates to the profile on paper; no feeding trial required.
  • Animal feeding tests using AAFCO procedures substantiate that [product] provides complete and balanced nutrition for [life stage] — an actual AAFCO-protocol feeding trial was run (typically 26 weeks for adult maintenance, 10 weeks for growth).
  • Product family member — one product in the family was tested and the others inherit the claim through formula similarity.
  • Intended for intermittent or supplemental feeding only — this is the opposite of complete. It is the single most useful red flag on a label.

The statement must name the species and the life stage. That is the only nutrition claim on the packaging a buyer can actually verify; everything else (natural, human-grade, vet recommended) carries no legal guarantee of nutritional adequacy.

Hong Kong context: there is no local nutritional standard for pet food. Consumer protection runs through the Trade Descriptions Ordinance (Cap. 362), which addresses false or misleading claims rather than nutrient adequacy. In practice, complete and balanced claims on products sold here reference AAFCO (US) or FEDIAF (Europe), and nobody local audits them. Being able to read the statement yourself beats trusting the packaging design.

Life stages: growth, adult maintenance, and all life stages

The same brand and formula name may ship in several life-stage versions, and the thresholds differ substantially:

  • Growth / reproduction — the highest bar. Puppies, pregnant and lactating bitches need more protein, calcium, phosphorus, vitamin D, and energy density because bone and tissue are being built fast.
  • Adult maintenance — the lowest bar: maintain weight and normal function.
  • All life stages — the product clears both the growth/reproduction and adult profiles, so in practice it is built to the higher (growth) threshold. For a neutered adult dog this is usually not harmful, but energy and some minerals come with headroom, so watch body condition.

The most common and most expensive mistake: a puppy, especially a large-breed puppy, eating a diet labelled adult maintenance only. Absolute calcium and the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio fall short, and the consequence is skeletal — often invisible for months, by which time it is structural.

Comparing numbers: per 1000 kcal versus dry matter

This is the most practically useful technical point in the article. Canned and fresh diets are roughly 75–80% water; dry kibble is around 10%. So "protein 10%" on a can cannot be compared with "protein 26%" on a bag — most of the can is water.

  • Dry matter (DM) basis: subtract the water, then divide the percentage by (1 − moisture fraction). This compares concentration. The AAFCO profiles include DM columns.
  • Per 1000 kcal ME: compares how much the dog actually eats relative to energy. This is the primary column in the AAFCO profiles. Why energy as the denominator? Because dogs eat to an energy requirement, not to a weight of food. A 5 kg dog eating a few hundred kcal a day and a 30 kg dog eating over a thousand are not consuming the same absolute amount at the same percentage.
  • Practical trap: homemade recipes are usually written per kilogram of food or per portion, with no energy density stated. To check one properly you must run the ingredients through nutrition software or a composition database (USDA FoodData Central, for example) to get total calories, then convert to amounts per 1000 kcal before anything can be compared to a profile.

Protein and amino acids: a minimum percentage is not sufficiency

The AAFCO minimum for crude protein is roughly 18% DM for adult maintenance and about 22.5% for growth. Those numbers guarantee quantity, not quality.

  • Dogs require around ten essential amino acids (arginine, histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, valine), plus taurine-related considerations during growth.
  • The AAFCO profiles set individual minimums for amino acids, not just crude protein. So "30% protein must be plenty" is a bad inference: if the main protein sources are skin, tendon, and feet — high in collagen — the amino acid profile can be poor even with a high total number.
  • Processing and bioavailability matter too. The same protein, cooked versus raw, or from different species, differs measurably in how much of each amino acid the dog can actually use. Profile numbers are a floor, not a quality score.

The nutrients homemade fresh diets most often miss

The strongest primary data here is Stockman et al., published in JAVMA in 2013: of 200 home-prepared maintenance recipes for adult dogs, 95% had at least one essential nutrient below NRC or AAFCO standards and 83.5% had multiple deficiencies. Only nine recipes met AAFCO. All four recipes written by board-certified veterinary nutritionists were complete — that contrast is the finding.

  • Zinc — deficient in 69% of recipes, the most common gap. Zinc absorption from meat is affected by phytate, calcium, and copper; chicken breast plus white rice is almost guaranteed to fall short.
  • Choline — deficient in 64.5%. Egg yolk and liver are rich sources; lean-muscle-only recipes tend to miss it.
  • Copper — deficient in 54%.
  • EPA + DHA — deficient in 53.5%. These must come from fish oil or oily fish; ALA from flax converts very poorly in dogs and is not an equivalent substitute.
  • Calcium — deficient in 35%, but the more dangerous pattern is a skewed calcium-to-phosphorus ratio: all-meat recipes run high in phosphorus and low in calcium, and in puppies the skeletal effect is immediate.
  • The other direction carries risk too. The same study found recipes exceeding the safe upper limit for vitamin D and for EPA/DHA, and heavy long-term liver feeding causes vitamin A excess. Homemade diets fail by overshooting as well as undershooting.
  • Hong Kong context: hot and humid. Cooked fresh food should spend minimal time at room temperature, portions should be refrigerated and used within a few days, and longer storage belongs in the freezer. Mould growth and fat oxidation degrade nutrients that were calculated correctly on paper, so getting the numbers right and storing the food right are two halves of the same job.

Checking a recipe against the AAFCO profile — and when to call a nutritionist

  • Step 1: establish energy. Estimate daily calorie needs from body weight and activity (the RER/MER approach used in clinical nutrition). Without an energy baseline, nothing downstream is comparable.
  • Step 2: run the numbers. Enter the weight of every ingredient into nutrition software or a composition database to get total calories and total nutrients. Hand-checking a few majors (calcium, phosphorus, zinc, calories) is feasible; a full audit is not.
  • Step 3: convert to per 1000 kcal. Compare each nutrient against the AAFCO adult maintenance minimum — and against the maximum, because exceeding an upper limit is also non-compliance.
  • Step 4: check dry matter concentration. Confirm you are not looking at a pass created by water dilution, or a fail created by concentration.
  • Step 5: ask the three questions a profile cannot answer. The amino acid profile (not just crude protein), fatty acid ratios, and the bioavailability of each mineral source. These are where software is most likely to mislead and where real outcomes are decided.
  • Step 6: monitor over time. Body condition score, weight, coat and skin, stool quality, annual bloodwork. Any change to the recipe — different meat, different supplement brand — means recalculating; one audit is not permanent.

Do not improvise in these situations: puppies and large-breed growth, pregnancy and lactation, any chronic disease (kidney, heart, pancreas, urinary stones, skin or gut allergy), long-term home-cooked feeding as the main diet, raw feeding, or basing the staple diet on an internet recipe. Those need a board-certified veterinary nutritionist (DACVIM or DECVCN), not a general practitioner or a pet shop assistant. One consultation buys years of skeletal, kidney, and cardiac health — the highest-return line item in any home-cooking budget.

References

  • AAFCO. AAFCO Official Publication (updated annually; includes the Dog and Cat Food Nutrient Profiles and model regulations). Association of American Feed Control Officials.
  • AAFCO. AAFCO Methods for Substantiating Nutritional Adequacy of Dog and Cat Foods (including feeding trial protocols).
  • National Research Council. Nutrient Requirements of Dogs and Cats. Washington, DC: National Academies Press; 2006.
  • WSAVA Global Nutrition Committee. Global Nutrition Guidelines and Guidelines on Selecting Pet Foods (continuously updated). World Small Animal Veterinary Association.
  • Freeman LM, Becvarova I, Cave N, et al. WSAVA Nutritional Assessment Guidelines. Journal of Small Animal Practice. 2011;52(7):385–396.
  • Stockman J, Fascetti AJ, Kass PH, Larsen JA. Evaluation of recipes of home-prepared maintenance diets for dogs. Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association. 2013;242(11):1500–1505.
  • FEDIAF. Nutritional Guidelines for Complete and Complementary Pet Food for Cats and Dogs (European counterpart, updated annually).

title: 狗狗行為解讀手冊
title_en: How to Read Your Dog's Behaviour — A Practical Body-Language Handbook
source: 改編自KCAEA HK寵物課程筆記＋一手行為學來源
source_en: Adapted from KCAEA HK pet course notes + primary behaviour sources
disclaimer: 本文為一般教育資訊，並非獸醫診斷。行為突然改變可能係身體不適，請諮詢註冊獸醫。
disclaimer_en: General educational information only — not veterinary advice. Sudden behaviour change can signal pain or illness; consult a registered veterinarian.
desc_en: A wagging tail is not a friendly tail, and a rolled-over belly is not always submission. A body-language handbook built on veterinary behaviour sources — tail height and speed, ears, weight shifts, stress clusters, play bows, food guarding and barking — plus the Hong Kong flat, lift and dog-park situations where reading goes wrong.
content_html:
一句總結：讀狗唔係查字典。同一個動作，喺唔同情境可以代表完全相反嘅情緒；同一個情緒，喺唔同品種身上又可以顯示到幾乎認唔出。真正可靠嘅讀法，係把尾巴、耳仔、眼、口同身體重心當成一組訊號，連埋現場情境一齊睇。

以下七段，每段都可以獨立抽出嚟做一條短片：尾巴、耳仔同面部微訊號（包括打呵欠同舔唇）、身體重心同僵硬、遊戲 bow、護食、吠叫，最後一段講最重要嘅一件事 —— 行為突然改變，首先要排除痛楚。

  • 睇整體：任何單一部位都唔可以獨立斷症，尾巴同耳仔要同身體一齊讀。
  • 睇情境：同樣一個舔唇動作，食完飯同喺獸醫診所意思完全唔同。
  • 睇變化：最有用嘅比較對象，係「呢隻狗平日嘅樣」，唔係「一般狗應該點」。

香港嘅居住環境令呢件事特別難：單位細、走廊窄、升降機要同陌生狗貼身、狗公園一到週末就密集，打風落雨又可能連續幾日冇得散步。以下每段都會指出香港情境下最常出問題嘅位。

尾巴：高度、速度、方向，三樣要一齊睇

神話：搖尾就係友善、想玩。

實證：搖尾代表嘅係「喚醒程度上升」同「有社交意圖」，唔係一個固定嘅情緒標籤。同一條尾，可以係想繼續玩，可以係想叫對方停，亦可以係衝突前嘅最後訊號。獸醫行為專科醫生喺 VCA 醫院嘅文章講得好白：好多狗隻喺被陌生人摸嘅時候，條尾一直擺，但意思係「我唔想再繼續」；呢種誤讀，有時會以吠咬收場。

  • 高位、變硬、tight arch 過背：喚醒度同自信上升，可以升級成攻擊展示。
  • 低位快速擺：唔係開心。恐懼嘅狗一樣會擺得快，只係條尾收得好低。
  • 中性稍高、溫和擺動：對眼前事物有興趣，想繼續互動。
  • 停擺加全身僵硬：呢個係「暫停」訊號，意思係「停手」。

品種基準線差好遠：比高犬放鬆時條尾本身就舉高，格力犬同惠比特會收落肚，西伯利亞雪橇就捲上背。剪尾或者天生短尾嘅狗，等於少咗一個遠距離訊號，要靠面部同身體補位。

仲有方向。意大利團隊做過實驗：狗見到主人時，尾巴偏向自己右邊擺；見到陌生或者有威脅性嘅狗時，偏向左邊。之後佢哋再播片俾其他狗睇，狗隻對「左擺」嘅反應明顯緊張 —— 心率上升、夾尾、撐腿，甚至行開。呢個發現好有趣，但唔好當成日常工具：喺街上面用肉眼分左右擺，可靠度遠低於老老實實睇整體姿勢。

可以點拍：同一隻狗三個片段 —— 屋企放鬆、主人返屋企、街上面遇到陌生狗，用慢鏡標出尾巴高度同速度嘅差別。

香港嘅行人路同公園通道窄，兩隻狗迎面相遇時好難拉開距離，所以喺呢啲位置要特別早讀訊號。

耳仔、眼白、舔唇、打呵欠：最早出現嘅四個訊號

耳位係最快、最易被忽略嘅訊號，前提係你知道呢隻狗「放鬆時對耳仔係點」。立耳狗向前傾，代表專注或者警覺；向後貼，代表恐懼或者準備防禦。垂耳狗嘅耳根一樣會向後拉，只係冇咁明顯。

有一點香港狗主好少留意：你隻狗嘅外形本身可能令佢「講唔清」。Dogs Trust 指出，深色毛同長毛會蓋住細微動作，垂耳令耳仔動作冇咁明顯，皺皮或者過緊嘅皮膚限制面部同身體活動，短吻品種做唔出多種表情，捲得太緊嘅尾亦好難表達情緒；而呢啲特徵好多同時伴隨健康問題。即係話，一隻法國鬥牛或者八哥「冇乜表情」，唔一定係佢淡定。

要練嘅三個細節：眼白（頭唔轉、眼球側望，見到明顯眼白，俗稱 whale eye）、瞳孔（光線冇變但放大）、嘴角（向後拉長、嘴唇閉緊，同放鬆時微微張開嘅嘴唔同）。神話：狗「笑」就等於友善 —— 狗冇人類式嘅社交笑容；張嘴、舌頭外露多數係散熱或者喘氣，要睇氣溫同活動量。

再上一層係打呵欠、舔鼻、舔唇、突然好有興趣咁聞地下、動作變慢、身體側向、頭轉開。呢啲喺訓練界常被統稱 calming signals，源自挪威訓犬師 Turid Rugaas 嘅觀察。呢個框架實務上好好用，因為佢提醒狗主：狗好少一開始就用吠咬溝通，佢會先用一堆細動作叫你收手。

但要講清楚極限：以上任何一個動作，單獨出現都唔可以斷症。狗起身會打呵欠，食完會舔唇，行過有味嘅地方會突然低頭狂聞。可靠嘅讀法係三樣一齊 —— 集群（兩三個訊號同時出現）、情境（現場有冇壓力源）、變化（同佢平日比）。「睇整體、睇情境」呢個原則，獸醫行為科同主要動物福利機構嘅指引都一致。

香港情境：升降機係最典型嘅例子。兩隻陌生狗喺一平方米內被迫貼身，好多時「突然」吠或者撲，其實前面已經有幾秒訊號：頭轉開、舔鼻、眼白、身體側向門口。隻狗一直喺講「我想走」，只係冇位走。其餘兩個高頻情境係獸醫診所等候區（氣味、陌生狗、被抱上枱），同打風落雨連續幾日冇得出街（能量累積、環境單調）。

唔好做：見到舔唇就話「佢驚我」，然後強行抱實安慰。對一隻想拉開距離嘅狗，擁抱係加大壓力。

身體重心、僵硬同「凍結」

重心向前，代表想接近；向後坐、體重壓落後腳，代表準備退。呢個分別喺狗公園入口最實用：一隻重心向後、但又被主人拉住向前嘅狗，正正係最容易爆發嘅狀態 —— 佢想走，但走唔到。

最被低估嘅危險訊號係「凍結」：成隻狗突然唔動、四腳撐實、定睛望住目標、嘴閉緊。呢個唔係服從，係高度衝突。行為科文獻講得好清楚，狗可以藉住停低成個身體、僵住條尾去中斷一個互動；而呢個「暫停」被忽略，就係衝突升級嘅常見起點。

豎毛要小心解讀：佢代表喚醒度上升，唔一定代表攻擊，亦唔等於「嬲」。要睇佢同時係向前定向後。

可以點拍：用牽繩張力做主題 —— 鬆繩、微緊、拉直三個狀態，配上狗嘅重心位置。香港走廊同狹窄行人路，好多時係條繩令狗「被逼」接近。

遊戲 bow 同邀玩：點分「玩」同「唔係玩」

遊戲 bow 嘅結構好清楚：前半身趴低、前腳伸直、屁股同尾舉高。呢個姿勢喺狗與狗、狗與人之間都會出現，而且唔止用嚟開始玩。

行為學家 Marc Bekoff 分析犬科動物嘅社交玩耍，提出 play signal 嘅作用好似「標點符號」：玩嘅中途，動作可能變得同打架、捕獵好似，狗會插入一個 bow 或者類似訊號，重新標記「呢個仍然係玩」。呢個解釋咗一個常見現象 —— 玩到一半突然 bow 一下，然後繼續追。

真玩嘅指標：輪流（唔係一邊永遠追、一邊永遠逃）、動作誇張、張口但唔咬實、有暫停、讓賽（大隻嗰隻會就住細隻）。

唔係玩：被追嗰方冇再邀、冇 bow、夾尾、尖叫、躲去枱底；其中一隻愈來愈僵硬；體型差好遠而大嗰隻完全唔讓。

香港狗公園實務：入閘前先喺外面觀察三十秒，睇在場狗嘅互動質素，唔好一入閘就放繩。細單位養嘅狗，好多時未學識「退場」—— 屋企冇空間練，去到公園一被包圍，就只剩 fight 或者 freeze 兩個選擇。

護食同資源守護：最早出現嘅訊號係「快」

神話：護食嘅狗「惡」，要壓佢，要拎走個碗教佢規矩。

實證：獸醫行為學把食物相關攻擊同佔有性攻擊（資源守護）分開處理，兩者都係圍繞資源嘅正常防禦行為被強化或者泛化嘅結果。Merck Veterinary Manual 亦明確指出：對家庭成員嘅攻擊常被誤稱為「支配性攻擊」，但最常見嘅原因其實係恐懼、資源佔有、轉移行為，或者動機衝突。

早期訊號通常係「快」：食得快、身體側住遮住個碗、耳仔向後、眼白、你行過就停食盯住你、食嘢時成個身變硬。呢啲全部喺低吼之前出現。低吼係警告，唔係叛變。

唔好做：伸手入碗、突然搶走、懲罰低吼。懲罰只會令警告消失，唔會令動機消失 —— 結果係一隻唔再警告就直接咬嘅狗。

香港細單位可以點做：分房或者用圍欄分區餵食、食完即收碗、增加你行過同「好事發生」嘅連結、高價值食物只喺固定安全位置出現、小朋友同狗食嘢嘅區域完全分開。

如果已經有咬傷或者撲咬，唔好自己練。要獸醫先排除痛楚，再轉介行為專業。

吠叫：情境有分別，但唔等於可以逐句翻譯

「吠聲翻譯」唔可靠，但吠聲有情境特異性，係有實證嘅。Yin 同 McCowan 喺 2004 年發表嘅研究，錄咗 10 隻狗、共 4,672 個吠聲，分三個情境：陌生人撳門鐘、狗被隔離喺門外或者房間、同人或者另一隻狗玩。

結果：門鐘情境嘅吠聲多數粗糙、低頻、冇調制，持續時間長、重複密；隔離同玩嘅吠聲傾向較高頻、有音調變化、較 tonal。統計分析可以按情境把吠聲分類，即使同一隻狗都分得出。

所以有兩點要同時講：一，吠叫唔係純粹「引注意」，佢帶住情境資訊；二，呢個唔等於可以逐句翻譯。研究講嘅係統計上嘅傾向，唔係「呢一聲代表肚餓」。

香港嘅觸發通常好固定：走廊腳步聲、鄰居裝修、窗外風雨聲、升降機開門聲。呢啲重複而且可預測嘅觸發，正正係最值得記錄嘅對象。

比任何 App 有用嘅做法：錄音加記錄。每次吠叫記低時間、觸發（走廊腳步聲？鄰居裝修？窗外面積水？）、持續幾久、停唔停得返。三日之後你就會見到模式，而模式才係訓練嘅起點。

可以點拍：同一個門鐘觸發，錄三次吠叫，把聲譜並排，睇粗糙同 tonal 嘅分別。

行為突然改變：先當痛楚處理，幾時要睇獸醫

呢段係全文最重要嘅一段。AAHA 同 AAFP 嘅痛楚管理指引講得好直接：動物唔能夠用言語表達，行為改變目前係痛楚同療效最主要嘅指標。而 AAHA 嘅行為管理指引亦要求：處理行為問題之前，要先排除同治療可能嘅潛在疾病。

呢個唔係保守說法。Mills 等人在 2020 年嘅回顧中，檢視幾位作者近期 100 個狗嘅轉介個案，得出一個保守估計：大約三分之一個案涉及某種痛楚狀況，部分情況可能接近八成。骨科、腸胃、皮膚問題，都可以係行為問題嘅底層原因。

要即刻約獸醫嘅變化：

  • 突然唔肯上樓梯、唔跳梳化、上車要人抱
  • 唔俾人摸某個位，或者摸到某處會突然低吼
  • 室內大小便、夜間坐立不安、睡眠明顯改變
  • 食慾或者飲水明顯改變
  • 對熟悉嘅家人或者同伴狗突然唔友善
  • 行街突然唔肯行、怕聲、怕某種地面

香港特別容易睇漏兩樣：唐樓同舊樓嘅樓梯（狗每日要行，痛楚會最先出現喺上樓梯），同滑地板（關節痛嘅狗會避開或者打滑，好多主人以為係「唔想入廚房」）。

「觀察下先」係最貴嘅決定。行為突變唔係性格問題，係一個需要排除醫療原因嘅臨床問題。

The short version: reading a dog is not a lookup table. The same movement can mean opposite things in different contexts, and the same emotion can look almost unrecognisable across breeds. Reliable reading means treating tail, ears, eyes, mouth and weight distribution as one signal set, and reading that set against the situation in front of you.

The seven sections below each work as a standalone short video: the tail, the ears and facial micro-signals (including yawning and lip licking), weight and freezing, the play bow, food guarding, barking, and finally the thing that matters most — a sudden behaviour change is a medical question first.

  • Read the whole dog. No single body part diagnoses anything on its own.
  • Read the context. A lip lick after dinner and a lip lick in a vet waiting room are not the same event.
  • Read the change. The useful comparison is this dog's normal, not what dogs are supposed to look like.

Hong Kong makes this harder than most places: small flats, narrow corridors, lifts where strange dogs are pressed together, crowded dog parks at weekends, and typhoon days that can wipe out walks for several days in a row. Each section flags where it goes wrong here.

The tail: height, speed and direction all matter

The myth: a wagging tail means friendly and playful.

The evidence: wagging signals rising arousal and social intent — not a fixed emotion. The same tail can mean "keep playing", "stop that", or "this is about to go wrong". Veterinary behaviour specialists at VCA put it plainly: a dog being petted by a stranger may wag the whole time while actually asking for the interaction to end, and that misreading sometimes ends in a snap or a bite.

  • High, stiff, arched over the back: arousal and confidence climbing, and it can escalate into a full aggressive display.
  • Low and fast: not happy. A fearful dog wags quickly too — the tail is just carried low.
  • Neutral-to-slightly-raised, gentle wag: interested, wants to keep interacting.
  • Wag stops, body stiffens: a pause signal. It means stop.

Breed baselines vary enormously: beagles carry their tails high at rest, greyhounds and whippets tuck them under, huskies curl them over the back. Dogs with docked or naturally short tails have lost one long-distance channel and have to compensate with face and body.

Then there is direction. An Italian team found that dogs wag with a bias to their own right when they see their owner, and to their left when they see an unfamiliar or threatening dog. When other dogs watched video of left- versus right-biased wags, the left wag produced clear stress responses — higher heart rate, tucked tails, braced legs, sometimes leaving the room. It is a genuinely interesting finding, and a poor everyday tool: judging wag asymmetry by eye on a pavement is far less reliable than simply reading the whole posture.

Shoot this: three clips of the same dog — relaxed at home, owner coming home, meeting a strange dog on the street — with slow motion on tail height and speed.

Hong Kong pavements and park paths are narrow, so two dogs meeting head-on often cannot create distance — which is exactly where reading early matters most.

Ears, eye white, lip licks, yawns: the four earliest signals

Ear position is the fastest signal and the easiest to miss, but only against a baseline: you need to know how this dog holds its ears when relaxed. A prick-eared dog tipping its ears forward is alert and engaged; ears pinned back mean fear or a dog preparing to defend itself. A drop-eared dog pulls its ear bases back the same way — it is just harder to see.

One thing Hong Kong owners rarely consider: the dog's own shape may stop it communicating clearly. Dogs Trust notes that dark coats and long fur hide small movements, floppy ears make ear movement less visible, wrinkled or tight skin restricts the face and body, short-muzzled breeds have fewer facial expressions available, and tightly curled tails are hard to read — and many of those features travel with health problems. A French bulldog or a pug with "no expression" is not necessarily a calm dog.

Three details worth training your eye on: eye white (head still, eyeballs sliding sideways, a clear crescent of sclera — "whale eye"), pupils (dilated when the light has not changed), and mouth corners (drawn back and lips clamped, versus the soft slightly-open mouth of a relaxed dog). The myth: a dog "smiling" is a friendly dog. Dogs have no human social smile; an open mouth with the tongue out is usually thermoregulation — judge it against temperature and activity.

One layer subtler: yawning, nose licking, lip licking, sudden intense sniffing of the floor, movements slowing down, body turned away, head turned away. Trainers group these as "calming signals", a framework from the Norwegian trainer Turid Rugaas. It is useful because it reminds owners that dogs rarely open with a bark or a bite — they start with a stack of small requests to back off.

The limits, stated plainly: none of these diagnose anything alone. Dogs yawn when they get up, lick their lips after eating, and drop their heads to sniff something interesting. Reliable reading needs all three of: clustering (two or three signals together), context (is a stressor present), and change (how this compares with the dog's normal). Veterinary behaviour texts and the major welfare charities land on the same rule — read the whole body, in context.

Hong Kong context: the lift is the classic case. Two strange dogs pressed into one square metre, and the "sudden" bark or lunge is usually preceded by several seconds of signals — head turned away, nose lick, eye white, body angled towards the door. The dog has been saying "I want out" the whole time; it just has nowhere to go. The other two high-frequency situations are the vet waiting room (smells, strange dogs, being lifted onto a table) and three or four consecutive typhoon days with no walk (accumulated energy, a very dull environment).

Don't: see a lip lick, decide "he's scared of me", and hug the dog. For a dog trying to create distance, a hug increases the pressure.

Weight shift, stiffness and freezing

Weight forward means the dog wants to close the distance. Weight back, sitting into the hind legs, means it is preparing to retreat. This is the single most useful thing to read at a dog park gate: a dog whose weight is back but whose owner is pulling it forward is in the highest-risk configuration there is — it wants to leave and cannot.

The most under-rated danger signal is freezing: the dog stops moving, plants all four feet, locks onto the target and clamps its mouth. That is not obedience; it is acute conflict. The behavioural literature is explicit that dogs can interrupt an interaction by stilling the whole body and stiffening the tail, and that ignoring this pause is a common starting point for escalation.

Read raised hackles carefully: it means arousal is up. It does not mean aggression, and it does not mean "angry". Check whether the dog is leaning forward or back at the same time.

Shoot this: leash tension as the subject — slack, slightly tight, fully taut — with the dog's weight position in frame. In Hong Kong corridors and narrow pavements, tension is often what forces the approach.

The play bow: telling play from not-play

The structure is unmistakable: front end down, forelegs extended, rear end and tail up. It appears between dogs and between dogs and people, and it is not only used to start play.

The behavioural scientist Marc Bekoff analysed social play in canids and argued that play signals work like punctuation: mid-play, actions can start to look like fighting or hunting, and a dog inserts a bow or similar signal to re-mark "this is still play". That explains the familiar pattern of a bow in the middle of a chase, followed by more chasing.

Signs of real play: turn-taking (not one dog chasing and one dog fleeing for the entire time), exaggerated movements, open mouths without actual biting, pauses, and self-handicapping — the bigger dog holding back.

Not play: the chased dog never re-invites, never bows, tucks its tail, yelps, hides under a bench; one dog gets progressively stiffer; the size gap is large and the bigger dog gives nothing back.

Hong Kong dog park practice: watch from outside the gate for thirty seconds and assess the quality of what is already happening before you go in, and do not unclip the lead at the gate. Dogs raised in small flats often never learn how to exit an interaction — there is no space to practise at home, so in a park, once surrounded, the only options left are fight or freeze.

Food guarding: the earliest signal is speed

The myth: a dog that guards its food is "dominant" and needs to be put in its place — take the bowl away and teach it manners.

The evidence: veterinary behaviour treats food-related aggression and possessive aggression (resource guarding) as distinct categories, both of them normal defensive behaviour around a resource that has been reinforced or generalised. The Merck Veterinary Manual is explicit that aggression towards family members is often mistakenly labelled dominance aggression, when the usual drivers are fear, resource possession, redirected behaviour, or conflict between two competing motivations.

The early signals are about speed: eating faster, body curved over the bowl, ears back, eye white, freezing and staring when you walk past, the whole body going hard while eating. All of that comes before a growl. A growl is a warning, not a coup.

Don't: put a hand in the bowl, snatch it away, or punish the growl. Punishment removes the warning without removing the motivation — which produces a dog that bites without warning.

What works in a small Hong Kong flat: feed in separate rooms or behind a barrier, pick the bowl up when the meal is finished, build a positive association with you walking past, keep high-value food to one safe predictable spot, and keep children entirely out of the dog's eating area.

If there has already been a bite or a lunge, do not train it yourself. A vet rules out pain first, then refers to a behaviour professional.

Barking: context matters, but it is not a translation app

Bark-translator apps are not reliable, but the fact that barks carry context information is well evidenced. Yin and McCowan recorded 10 dogs and 4,672 barks across three situations: a stranger ringing the doorbell, the dog isolated outside or in another room, and play with a person or another dog.

The results: doorbell barks tended to be harsh, low-frequency and unmodulated, longer, and repeated more rapidly. Isolation and play barks tended to be higher-pitched, more modulated and more tonal. Discriminant analysis could sort barks by context even within a single dog.

Two conclusions have to be held together. One: barking is not merely attention-seeking — it carries situational information. Two: that is not the same as translating individual barks. The study describes statistical tendencies, not "this bark means hungry".

In Hong Kong the triggers are usually very consistent: footsteps in the corridor, a neighbour's renovation, wind and rain against the window, the lift door. Repeated, predictable triggers are exactly what is worth logging.

What beats any app: record and log. Note the time, the trigger (footsteps in the corridor? the neighbour's renovation? water hitting the window?), the duration, and whether the dog could stop. Three days of that and you have a pattern, and the pattern is where training starts.

Shoot this: one doorbell trigger, three recordings, spectrograms side by side showing harsh versus tonal.

Sudden behaviour change: treat it as pain first

This is the most important section in the article. The AAHA/AAFP pain management guidelines state it directly: because animals cannot report pain verbally, behavioural change is currently the principal indicator of pain and of how treatment is progressing. The AAHA behaviour management guidelines require the same order of operations — underlying medical conditions must be identified and treated before behavioural treatment begins.

This is not defensive caution. In a 2020 review, Mills and colleagues examined 100 recent dog referrals across several authors' caseloads and gave a conservative estimate that around a third involved some form of painful condition, with the figure approaching 80% in some instances. Orthopaedic, gastrointestinal and dermatological disease can all sit underneath what looks like a behaviour problem.

Book a vet for any of these:

  • Suddenly refusing stairs, no longer jumping onto the sofa, needing to be lifted into the car
  • Not tolerating touch in one area, or growling when a specific spot is reached
  • Indoor toileting, restlessness at night, changed sleep
  • Marked change in appetite or water intake
  • Sudden unfriendliness towards familiar family members or a housemate dog
  • Stopping on walks, new sound sensitivity, refusing certain surfaces

Two things get missed constantly in Hong Kong: stairs in walk-up buildings (dogs climb them daily, so pain shows up there first), and smooth tiled floors (a dog with joint pain avoids them or skids — often read as "he just doesn't want to come into the kitchen").

"Let's watch it for a while" is the most expensive decision available. A sudden behaviour change is not a personality problem. It is a clinical question that needs medical causes excluded.

title: 狗狗急救與緊急事故手冊
title_en: The Dog First-Aid & Emergency Handbook — What to Do in the Golden Hour
content_html:
一句話重點：狗狗急症唔係靠運氣，係靠頭十分鐘你做對幾件事 —— 唔好亂搬、唔好亂催吐、記住時間、即刻打電話。以下七個最常見嘅家居急症，每個都可以獨立睇。

香港嘅居住環境有幾個特別風險：高樓、窄𨋢、夏天又熱又濕、屋企同屋苑常備老鼠藥同清潔劑。以下每一步都寫明「幾時要即刻去醫院」，唔會叫你喺屋企估。

黃金一小時：先做三件事，唔好做第四件

第一，確保自己安全：馬路上嘅車流、碎玻璃、電線、另一隻受驚嘅狗，都會令你變成第二個傷者。第二，打電話去急症醫院，講明幾分鐘後到、隻狗咩事、大約幾重 —— AVMA 明確建議先打電話，等醫院可以預備。第三，記時間：幾點食咗咩、食咗幾多、幾點開始抽。呢三個數字直接決定治療方案。

第四件唔好做：自己催吐。ASPCA 動物毒物控制中心講得好白：鹽、ipecac、用手指或物件挖喉都危險 —— 鹽可以令血鈉急升甚至抽筋，ipecac 可以引發嚴重心律問題。家用唯一可以安全催吐嘅方法係雙氧水，但一定要經獸醫指示先用，因為份量同禁忌（例如已經嘔緊、吞咗腐蝕性物質）都要專業判斷。

屋企急救包，放喺固定位置，全家都知喺邊：

  • 無菌紗布、自黏繃帶、透氣膠布
  • 鈍頭剪刀、鑷子、即棄手套
  • 生理鹽水（沖洗傷口、沖眼）
  • 數碼體溫計＋水溶性潤滑劑
  • 大毛巾或毯（可以即場做擔架）
  • 長繃帶或領巾（自製口套）
  • 即棄針筒（沖洗用）
  • 24 小時急症醫院地址同電話、狗隻病歷副本

紅旗徵狀：見到呢啲唔好等

Merck 獸醫手冊列出一批「唔理檢查結果、即刻送入治療區」嘅情況，主人版本可以照跟：呼吸困難、大量出血、昏迷或站唔起、抽搐、牙齦白或藍紫、腹脹兼乾嘔（疑似胃扭轉）、誤食毒物、創傷或開放性傷口、中暑。

要判斷「唔正常」，先要知正常：體溫 38.3–39.2°C、心跳每分鐘 70–120 下（小型犬偏快）、休息時呼吸每分鐘 18–34 次、牙齦按落去 1–2 秒內回復粉紅。牙齦灰白或藍紫，或者按完超過 2 秒都唔返色，代表灌流出問題，唔係「唞下就好」。

香港實務：大部分診所夜間同周日休息，急症要去指定醫院。預先喺手機存好最近嘅 24 小時急症醫院地址，唔好等到出事才 Google。

呼吸困難同哽塞：唔好伸手入喉

先分清咳嗽同哽塞：咳嗽係用力呼氣，但仍然吸到氣；哽塞係吸氣出事，狗會伸頸、張口、用胸腹大力抽氣、牙齦變色。VIN 獸醫第一手急救指引特別提醒：真正哽塞好少見，好多時只係咳嗽（例如犬舍咳），錯做急救反而整傷隻狗。

如果狗仍然企得穩、咳得應，保持冷靜、唔好按頸、唔好強行挖喉 —— 好容易被咬，亦可能將異物推得更深，即刻去獸醫。只有喺狗昏迷、而你確認睇得到異物先，才小心清出口腔；冇呼吸就開始救援呼吸同心外壓：單人 30 下胸壓配 2 口氣，胸壓速率每分鐘 100–120 下（2024 RECOVER 指引）。

短鼻品種（八哥、法鬥、北京犬）先天氣道窄，熱同興奮都會令呼吸急速惡化，送院門檻要比其他狗低。

中毒：朱古力、提子、木糖醇，同香港屋企嘅毒物

香港最常撞到嘅四類：朱古力（節日禮盒）、提子同提子乾（乾果、麥片、糕點）、木糖醇（無糖香口膠、喉糖、部分花生醬同牙膏）、老鼠藥。

  • 朱古力：毒素係可可鹼同咖啡因。Merck 數字：約 20 mg/kg 已經可以嘔吐肚瀉，40–50 mg/kg 影響心臟，60 mg/kg 或以上可以抽筋；牛奶朱古力約 62 g/kg 可能致命。黑朱古力同可可粉濃度可以高十倍以上（可可粉 28.5 mg/g，牛奶朱古力 2.3 mg/g），所以「食少少黑朱古力」都可以好嚴重。
  • 提子同提子乾：冇安全劑量。Merck 指每 4.5 kg 體重食多過一粒提子或提子乾，已經可能傷腎；腎衰竭可以喺 24–72 小時內出現，初期只係嘔同冇精神，好容易睇漏。
  • 木糖醇：超過 100 mg/kg 可以令血糖急跌（最快 30 分鐘內），超過 500 mg/kg 可以引致嚴重肝衰竭。所以買任何「無糖」食品前，睇成分表有冇 xylitol 或 E967。
  • 老鼠藥（抗凝血類）：最陰險。Merck 指凝血功能要 2–5 日後才見異常，出血通常 3–7 日後才出現 —— 隻狗今日精神奕奕，唔代表冇事，一定要即刻去驗。

通渠水、漂白水呢類腐蝕性物質，絕對唔好催吐（會二次灼傷食道）。正確做法：收好包裝、記低份量同時間、帶埋去診所，由獸醫決定是否需要洗胃、活性碳或留院。

中暑：香港夏天最快嘅急症

狗全身只有腳掌有汗腺，主要靠喘氣散熱（Cornell）。香港 5 至 8 月下午氣溫經常超過 31°C，夜間都成 26°C 而濕度極高 —— 濕度越高，喘氣蒸發越無效，所以夜晚散步一樣可以中暑。

最危險嘅係車廂：研究顯示車內溫度一小時內平均可以升 40°F（約 22°C），就算外面只係 21°C。香港「泊低五分鐘買杯嘢」都足以出事。

徵狀：狂喘、大量流口水、企唔穩、牙齦鮮紅或發紫、嘔、抽筋、倒下。體溫升到 105°F（約 40.6°C）或以上就係真急症，唔係普通「熱氣」。

要做：即刻離開熱源，去陰涼地方開風扇或冷氣；用凍水淋身（腳掌、耳翼、腹部），開車窗開冷氣送去醫院。有體溫計就量直腸溫，降到約 39.4°C（103°F）就停止主動降溫，避免降過龍。唔好蓋濕毛巾（會阻礙蒸發）；狗昏迷、抽筋、嘔緊或者抬唔起頭，就唔好浸水，改用淋水加風扇。亦唔好強行灌水入口。

流血、傷口同搬動受傷狗隻

外出血：用乾淨紗布或毛巾直接壓住傷口，至少壓 3 分鐘先好揭開睇（AVMA）。腳掌出血一般 5–10 分鐘止到；如果壓咗 10–15 分鐘仍然流，或者血係噴出嚟，即刻去急症（VCA）。紗布濕透都唔好拆，加一層繼續壓 —— 拆會整甩血塊。

傷口有深深插住嘅玻璃或異物，唔好拔，交由獸醫處理；一般擦傷可以用生理鹽水或清水沖走碎屑，再輕輕覆蓋。開放性骨折就相反：唔好沖洗傷口深處、唔好嘗試將骨推返入去，用無菌紗布或乾淨布覆蓋，直接送院（VIN）。

搬動：就算平時最乖，痛起上嚟都會咬 —— 先戴口罩（用長繃帶或領巾即場做），再用大板、摺枱板或厚毯做擔架，保持身體水平，唔好抱住或者夾住佢。除中暑外要保暖。住高樓嘅，找人幫手，唔好一個人抱住行樓梯。

抽搐：五分鐘定生死

抽搐超過 5 分鐘，或者 24 小時內抽多過一次（cluster seizure），就係需要即刻靜脈注射藥物嘅急症（Cornell）。抽搐本身會令體溫急升，拖得久可以造成不可逆嘅腦同器官損傷。

要做：即刻計時（手機計時器）、移開枱角同硬物、拉窗簾減光、保持安靜、用手機錄影 —— 獸醫靠呢條片判斷係唔係癲癇、由邊個腦區開始。

唔好做：唔好塞手指、匙羹或布入佢口（會咬斷牙、阻塞氣道，你亦會被咬）；唔好淋水；唔好成個人壓住佢；唔好喺抽搐期間餵藥或餵水。

抽完之後幾分鐘到幾小時係「postictal」階段，狗會迷茫、亂行、甚至兇人 —— 用牽繩或籠限制活動，唔好即刻抱。第一次抽、抽完十分鐘都企唔返、24 小時內再抽，或者本身有糖尿病、心臟病，一律即刻去醫院。

In one line: surviving a dog emergency is not luck — it is the first ten minutes done right: don't move what shouldn't be moved, don't make your dog vomit on your own, note the clock, and call ahead. Here are the seven most common household emergencies, each written to stand alone.

Hong Kong adds its own risks: high-rise flats, narrow lifts, hot and brutally humid summers, and rodenticide and cleaning chemicals kept in homes and common areas. Every step below says exactly when to stop trying at home and go to a hospital.

The golden hour: do three things, skip the fourth

First, make the scene safe for you: traffic, broken glass, live cables, or a second frightened dog can turn you into a second casualty. Second, call the emergency hospital before you drive — say when you will arrive, what happened, and roughly how much your dog weighs. The AVMA specifically advises calling ahead so the team can prepare. Third, write down the time: when your dog ate what, how much, and when the seizure started. Those three facts drive every treatment decision.

The fourth thing not to do: induce vomiting yourself. The ASPCA Animal Poison Control Center is blunt about this — salt, ipecac, and fingers or objects down the throat are all dangerous. Salt can push sodium to life-threatening levels and trigger seizures; ipecac can cause severe heart rhythm problems. The only home method that can be used safely is hydrogen peroxide, and only under veterinary direction, because the dose and the contraindications (already vomiting, swallowed a corrosive) need a professional call.

Build a first-aid kit, keep it in one fixed place, and make sure everyone in the household knows where it is:

  • Sterile gauze, self-adhesive bandage, medical tape
  • Blunt scissors, tweezers, disposable gloves
  • Saline (wound and eye rinsing)
  • Digital thermometer plus water-based lubricant
  • A large towel or blanket (an instant stretcher)
  • A long bandage or scarf (improvised muzzle)
  • Disposable syringes for flushing
  • The nearest 24-hour hospital's address and number, plus a copy of your dog's records

Red flags: when waiting is the wrong choice

The Merck Veterinary Manual lists the complaints that should go straight to the treatment area regardless of exam findings. The owner-level version: difficulty breathing, heavy bleeding, collapse or inability to stand, seizures, white or blue gums, a swollen abdomen with unproductive retching (possible bloat), toxin ingestion, trauma or open wounds, and heatstroke.

To judge "abnormal," know normal: temperature 101–102.5°F (38.3–39.2°C), heart rate 70–120 beats per minute (small dogs run faster), resting respiratory rate 18–34 breaths per minute, and gums that refill pink within 1–2 seconds of pressing. Gums that are pale, grey, or blue — or that stay pale for more than 2 seconds — mean poor perfusion, not "he just needs a rest."

Hong Kong reality check: most clinics close at night and on Sundays, and after-hours care means a specific hospital. Save the nearest 24-hour hospital in your phone now, not while your dog is bleeding on the floor.

Breathing trouble and choking: keep your fingers out of the throat

Separate coughing from choking. Coughing is a forceful exhale with air still getting in; choking is a problem on the inhale — neck extended, mouth open, chest and abdomen working hard, gums changing colour. VIN's veterinary first-aid guidance makes a point of this: true choking is rare, many "choking" dogs are actually coughing (kennel cough, for example), and first aid given to a coughing dog can cause injury.

If your dog is standing and coughing productively, stay calm, don't press on the neck, and don't go digging in the mouth — you will get bitten and you may push the object deeper. Go to the vet. Only if the dog is unconscious and you can actually see the object should you clear the mouth; if there is no breathing, start rescue breaths and compressions at 30 compressions to 2 breaths for a single rescuer, at 100–120 compressions per minute (2024 RECOVER guidelines).

Flat-faced breeds (pugs, French bulldogs, Pekingese) have narrow airways to begin with. Heat and excitement escalate fast, so their threshold for going in should be lower than other dogs'.

Poisoning: chocolate, grapes, xylitol and the toxins already in your flat

Four categories cover most Hong Kong cases: chocolate (holiday boxes), grapes and raisins (dried fruit, cereal, pastries), xylitol (sugar-free gum, mints, some peanut butters and toothpastes), and rodenticide.

  • Chocolate: the toxins are theobromine and caffeine. Merck's figures: about 20 mg/kg causes vomiting and diarrhoea, 40–50 mg/kg affects the heart, and 60 mg/kg or more can cause seizures; milk chocolate is potentially lethal at roughly 62 g/kg. Dark chocolate and cocoa powder are far more concentrated (cocoa powder 28.5 mg/g versus milk chocolate 2.3 mg/g), so "just a little dark chocolate" can be serious.
  • Grapes and raisins: there is no safe dose. Merck notes that more than one grape or raisin per 4.5 kg (10 lb) of body weight may be enough to injure the kidneys, and kidney failure can develop within 24–72 hours — early on it looks like nothing more than vomiting and lethargy.
  • Xylitol: over 100 mg/kg can crash blood sugar (within 30 minutes in some dogs), and over 500 mg/kg can cause severe liver failure. Check the label of anything marketed as sugar-free for xylitol or E967 before it comes into the house.
  • Rodenticide (anticoagulant type): the sneakiest one. Merck notes clotting tests become abnormal 2–5 days after ingestion and bleeding typically appears 3–7 days later. A dog that looks fine today is not fine — get it checked immediately.

Never induce vomiting after a corrosive like drain cleaner or bleach; it burns the oesophagus a second time. Instead, bag the packaging, note the amount and the time, and take it with you so the vet can decide between decontamination, charcoal, or admission.

Heatstroke: Hong Kong's fastest emergency

Dogs sweat only through their paw pads and rely on panting to cool down (Cornell). From May to August, Hong Kong afternoons routinely exceed 31°C (88°F), and nights still sit near 26°C (79°F) at very high humidity. The more humid the air, the less effective panting becomes — which is why a night walk can still end in heatstroke.

Cars are the worst case: research cited by Veterinary Partner found in-car temperature can rise by an average of 40°F (about 22°C) within an hour, even when it is only 70°F (21°C) outside. "Just five minutes to grab a coffee" is enough.

Signs: frantic panting, heavy drooling, wobbliness, bright red or purple gums, vomiting, seizures, collapse. A core temperature of 105°F (40.6°C) or above is a true emergency, not just "feeling hot."

What to do: get out of the heat, into shade with a fan or air conditioning, and pour cool water over the paws, ear flaps, and belly while you drive to the hospital with the windows down and the AC on. If you can take a rectal temperature, stop active cooling at about 103°F (39.4°C) so you don't overshoot. Do not wrap your dog in wet towels — it blocks evaporation. Do not immerse a dog that is unconscious, seizing, vomiting, or unable to hold its head up; keep wetting it and use a fan instead. Never force water into the mouth.

Bleeding, wounds, and moving an injured dog

External bleeding: press a clean cloth or gauze firmly on the wound and leave it there for at least three minutes before checking (AVMA). Paw bleeding usually stops in 5–10 minutes; if it is still bleeding after 10–15 minutes, or the blood is spurting, go to the emergency hospital (VCA). If the gauze soaks through, do not remove it — add another layer on top, because peeling it off dislodges the clot.

Glass or an object deeply embedded in a wound stays where it is; the vet removes it. Ordinary scrapes can be flushed with saline or clean water to clear debris, then covered lightly. Open fractures are the opposite: don't flush deep into the wound, don't try to push bone back in, cover it with sterile gauze or a clean cloth, and transport (VIN).

Moving the dog: even the gentlest dog bites when it is in pain, so muzzle first (a long bandage or scarf works), then slide a board, a folded table top, or a thick blanket under the dog as a stretcher and keep the body level. Don't carry or squeeze the dog against your body. Keep it warm except in heatstroke. In a high-rise, get a second person — do not carry a struggling dog down the stairs alone.

Seizures: five minutes decides the outcome

A seizure lasting more than five minutes, or more than one seizure within 24 hours (cluster seizures), is an emergency that needs intravenous medication (Cornell). The seizure itself drives body temperature up, and the longer it runs, the greater the risk of irreversible brain and organ damage.

What to do: start a timer, move furniture and hard objects away, dim the lights, keep the room quiet, and film it on your phone — the video helps the vet decide whether this is epilepsy and where in the brain it starts.

What not to do: don't put your fingers, a spoon, or cloth in the mouth (broken teeth, a blocked airway, and a bitten hand); don't pour water on the dog; don't lie across the body to hold it still; don't give food, water, or medication mid-seizure.

The minutes to hours afterwards are the postictal phase: disoriented, pacing, sometimes aggressive. Use a leash or a crate to limit movement and give the dog space. Go in immediately if this is the first seizure, if the dog cannot stand ten minutes later, if another seizure follows within 24 hours, or if your dog has diabetes or heart disease.

  • Hayes C. Xylitol Toxicosis in Dogs. Merck Veterinary Manual, updated Jun 2025.

title: 狗食物過敏致敏排行榜與排除飲食指南
source: 改編自 Mueller RS 等 (2016) BMC Vet Res 研究 + Dogalicious 實證整理
disclaimer: 本文內容整理自學術文獻與公開資料，經重新編寫加入原創分析。如有健康問題請諮詢註冊獸醫。排除飲食應在獸醫指導下進行。
content_html:
一句話重點：狗食物過敏要靠排除飲食確診，而非驗血或驗唾液——選一種全新蛋白，嚴格餵八週，再在獸醫指導下逐一重新挑戰。

致敏排行榜

一項針對犬隻皮膚型食物不良反應（CAFR）嘅回顧，整理咗 297 隻確診狗嘅資料，得出呢個排行榜：

排名致敏來源個案百分比
🥇牛肉10234%
🥈奶製品5117%
🥉雞肉4515%
4小麥3813%
5大豆186%
6羊肉145%
7粟米134%
8蛋114%
9豬肉72%
10魚52%
11米52%

唔係「牛肉有害」，而係「接觸得多」

呢個排行榜最容易被誤讀嘅地方，係將佢當成毒性排名。佢唔係。

食物過敏需要免疫系統先「認識」一種蛋白，先會對佢產生反應。同一種蛋白食得越多、食得越耐，被認住嘅機會就越高。牛肉同雞肉之所以位居榜首，正因為佢哋係市面上最普遍嘅狗糧蛋白——而唔係佢哋本身有問題。

呢個就係新穎蛋白（novel protein）嘅邏輯：揀一款你隻狗幾乎未食過嘅蛋白，令佢嘅免疫系統冇機會學會對佢反應。豬肉、魚、火雞、鹿肉、袋鼠肉都屬於呢類。

狗食物過敏係點樣形成嘅

狗食物過敏係免疫系統對食物中一種蛋白產生嘅反應——通常係一種中至大分子嘅醣蛋白，被免疫系統誤認為威脅。當中同時牽涉抗體介導與細胞介導嘅途徑，所以症狀可能喺進食後數小時甚至數日先出現。

呢個機制帶出兩個重要原則：

  • 必須曾經接觸 — 狗唔可能對從未食過嘅蛋白過敏。過敏往往是對熟悉嘅食物形成，而唔係對稀奇嘅食物。
  • 反應延遲而且會累積 — 由於部分屬細胞介導，今日偷食一次，可能到本週稍後先發作，呢個就係點解需要一個乾淨嘅試驗窗口。

分辨三個概念

  • 食物過敏 — 免疫系統對蛋白嘅反應，常見於皮膚與耳朵痕癢，有時伴腸胃症狀。只能靠排除飲食診斷。
  • 食物不耐受 — 非免疫性反應，例如難以消化高脂食材，通常只有腸胃症狀（軟便、脹氣）。
  • 環境過敏（異位性皮膚炎） — 對花粉、塵蟎或霉菌嘅反應，與食物無關，表現可以一模一樣。

排除飲食：八週逐週拆解

  1. 第 1–2 週：過渡與建立基線。皮膚未必有變化——你係喺清空系統，唔係期待奇蹟。
  2. 第 3–5 週：若食物係誘因，痕癢分數與耳炎通常開始緩和。
  3. 第 6–8 週：最清晰嘅判讀期。要嚴格記錄每週變化。
  4. 重新挑戰：加返舊糧，若 1-2 週內痕癢重現，診斷即告成立。

⚠️ 嚴格嘅開始：除咗試驗糧，唔可以俾任何其他蛋白來源——零食、潔齒骨、加味保健品、人類食物、朋友俾嘅火腿，全部要停。一粒芝士就足以令整個測試失效。

香港嘅現實

香港溫暖潮濕嘅氣候令皮膚屏障全年受壓，並助長繼發性酵母菌與細菌感染——狗狗嘅皮膚幾乎冇「淡季」可以復元。加上我哋嘅飲食文化習慣共享飯菜，嚴格的八週試驗需要真正的紀律。

title_en: Dog Food Allergy Rankings & Elimination Diet Guide — What the 2016 Mueller Study Actually Shows
desc_en: Beef, dairy, chicken top the list — not because they're toxic, but because dogs meet them most often. How to read the rankings and run a proper 8-week elimination diet.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Dog food allergy has to be diagnosed with an elimination diet, not a blood or saliva test. Pick one novel protein, feed it strictly for eight weeks, then — under vet supervision — challenge the old foods one at a time.

The allergen rankings

A review of canine cutaneous adverse food reactions (CAFR) pulled together data from 297 confirmed cases. Here's the ranking that came out:

RankAllergenCasesShare
🥇Beef10234%
🥈Dairy5117%
🥉Chicken4515%
4Wheat3813%
5Soy186%
6Lamb145%
7Corn134%
8Egg114%
9Pork72%
10Fish52%
11Rice52%

Not "beef is bad" — it's "exposure is high"

The most common way to misread this chart is to treat it like a toxicity ranking. It isn't.

Food allergy needs the immune system to first recognise a protein before it can react to it. The longer and more often your dog has eaten a protein, the more chances the immune system has to learn it. Beef and chicken sit at the top precisely because they're the most common proteins in commercial dog food — not because the proteins themselves are in any way harmful.

This is exactly the logic behind a novel protein: pick something your dog has barely or never eaten, so the immune system has had no chance to learn it. Pork, fish, turkey, venison, and kangaroo all fit that bucket.

How a dog food allergy actually forms

A canine food allergy is the immune system reacting to a protein in the food — usually a medium- to large-sized glycoprotein that the immune system mistakes for a threat. Both antibody-mediated and cell-mediated pathways are involved, which is why symptoms can show up hours or even days after a meal.

Two important principles follow from that:

  • Prior exposure is required. A dog cannot react to a protein it has never eaten. Allergies tend to develop against familiar foods, not exotic ones.
  • The reaction is delayed and cumulative. Because part of the response is cell-mediated, a single slip-up today may only flare later in the week — which is exactly why you need a clean testing window.

Three terms people mix up

  • Food allergy — immune reaction to a protein. Most often shows up as skin and ear itch, sometimes with gut symptoms. Can only be diagnosed with an elimination diet.
  • Food intolerance — non-immune, e.g. trouble digesting a high-fat food. Usually gut-only (loose stool, gas).
  • Environmental allergy (atopic dermatitis) — reaction to pollen, dust mites, or mould. Nothing to do with food, but the symptoms can look identical.

The elimination diet: 8 weeks, week by week

  1. Weeks 1–2: transition and baseline. The skin may not change — you're clearing the system, not expecting a miracle yet.
  2. Weeks 3–5: if food is the trigger, itch scores and ear infections usually start to ease.
  3. Weeks 6–8: the cleanest read. Track changes weekly.
  4. Re-challenge: reintroduce the old food. If the itch returns within 1–2 weeks, the diagnosis is locked in.

⚠️ A strict start: beyond the test food, no other protein source — no treats, no dental chews, no flavoured supplements, no human food, no well-meaning ham from a friend. A single cube of cheese is enough to invalidate the whole trial.

The Hong Kong reality

Hong Kong's warm, humid climate puts the skin barrier under pressure year-round and helps secondary yeast and bacterial infections take hold — dogs here barely get a quiet season for the skin to recover. Add a food culture that shares meals at the table, and an honest eight-week trial takes real discipline.

References

  1. Mueller RS, Olivry T, Prélaud P. Critically appraised topic on adverse food reactions of companion animals (2): common food allergen sources in dogs and cats. BMC Vet Res. 2016;12:9.
  2. Olivry T, Mueller RS. Critically appraised topic on adverse food reactions of companion animals (3): prevalence of cutaneous adverse food reactions in dogs and cats. BMC Vet Res. 2017;13:51.
  3. Cutaneous Food Allergy in Animals. Merck Veterinary Manual.
  4. AAFCO. Pet Food Labeling Guidelines.
  5. FDA. Complete and Balanced Pet Food Definitions.

title: 狗狗口臭點算？獸醫話你知真正原因同解決方法
source: 參考：NIH PMC9074277, PMC10981081, PMC7472411, BluePearl Vet
disclaimer: 本文僅供參考，如狗狗口臭持續或嚴重，請務必諮詢獸醫。排除飲食應在獸醫指導下進行。
content_html:
一句話重點：狗狗口臭唔係正常嘅事——可能係牙周病、腎功能問題（BUN偏高）或者飲食唔適合嘅警號，要對症處理先有效。

口臭係點樣形成嘅？

根據NIH研究（PMC9074277），狗口臭主要係因為口腔內細菌分解含硫胺基酸（半胱氨酸同甲硫氨酸）時產生嘅揮發性硫化物（VSCs）。呢啲化合物就係我哋聞到嘅難聞氣味。

研究顯示，狗牙周病嘅患病率高達44%至100%，係小動物臨床最常見嘅疾病之一。但牙周病唔係唯一原因。

四大成因分析

1. 牙周病（最常見）🥇

牙菌斑同牙石積聚，滋生大量厭氧細菌產生硫化物。牙周病唔止影響口腔，細菌仲可以進入血液，引發心臟、腎臟等其他器官問題。

2. 腎臟問題（BUN偏高）⚠️

腎功能受損嘅狗，血液中尿素氮（BUN）會升高。尿素會透過呼吸排出，產生類似氨水或尿味嘅口氣——學術上叫「uremic breath」。如果口臭帶有阿摩尼亞味，要即時驗血check腎功能。

3. 高蛋白飲食 🥩

研究顯示（PMC7472411），高蛋白飲食會改變狗嘅腸道菌群，增加蛋白質分解細菌。部分代謝產物透過呼吸排出，令口氣變差。羊肉、袋鼠肉呢類高蛋白紅肉影響尤其明顯。

4. 消化問題

腸胃消化不良、食物過敏或寄生蟲感染都可能導致口臭。食物喺腸道腐敗產生嘅氣體反流到口腔，就會有酸餿味。

參考案例：點心嘅情況

點心（18kg）嘅情況好有參考價值：

  • BUN偏高（2025-09血檢）→ 腎臟負荷要留意
  • 主食羊肉+袋鼠肉乾糧 → 高蛋白紅肉，代謝負擔大
  • 口臭+口水都臭 → 可能係腎源性（阿摩尼亞味）混合高蛋白飲食嘅結果

建議：先檢查牙齒有冇牙石，同時驗血覆檢BUN/CREA，確認口臭來源。

實戰建議

🪥 刷牙（最有效）

每日用寵物專用牙膏牙刷，研究證實可以顯著減少口臭。千祈唔好用人的牙膏（含氟有毒）。

🥬 飲食調整

  • BUN偏高 → 考慮轉低磷低蛋白主食，減少羊肉/袋鼠肉比例
  • 加入新鮮巴西利（parsley）切碎混糧，天然除口臭
  • 冷壓椰子油半茶匙溝糧，月桂酸抗菌
  • 益生菌繼續（你已經有俾），改善腸道菌群
  • 增加飲水（多放水碗/寵物飲水機）稀釋BUN

🏥 定期檢查

如果口臭持續或突然變嚴重，要做血常規（BUN/CREA）同牙科檢查。尤其係阿摩尼亞味嘅口臭，可能係腎病警號。

香港本地化

潮濕天氣：香港嘅潮濕氣候令口腔細菌滋生更快，要更勤力清潔水兜同玩具。

鮮食文化：好多香港狗主餵鮮食，但要留意蛋白質比例。如果好似點心咁食開羊肉+袋鼠肉，可以考慮溝低蛋白肉類（火雞、兔肉），或增加蔬菜比例。

  2. Effects of dental chew on halitosis in dogs. NIH. PMC10981081. 2024.
  3. Varying Protein Levels Influence Metabolomics and Gut Microbiota in Dogs. NIH. PMC7472411.

title_en: Why Does My Dog Have Bad Breath? A Vet Explains the Real Causes and What Actually Helps
desc_en: Dog bad breath is a warning sign — dental disease, kidney issues (high BUN), or the wrong diet. A vet breaks down the four real causes and the fixes that work.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Dog bad breath is not normal. It usually points to dental disease, kidney trouble (BUN running high), or a diet that doesn't suit your dog. Treating the symptom alone won't work — you have to find the source.

How does the smell actually form?

NIH research (PMC9074277) traces most doggy breath to volatile sulfur compounds (VSCs). Anaerobic bacteria in the mouth break down sulfur-containing amino acids (cysteine and methionine) and release these gases as a byproduct. That's the smell.

Studies put the rate of canine periodontal disease somewhere between 44% and 100%. It's one of the most common conditions vets see in small-animal practice. But gum disease isn't the only thing that stinks up a dog's mouth.

The four real causes

1. Periodontal disease (most common) 🥇

Plaque hardens into tartar. Anaerobic bacteria thrive under the gumline and pump out sulfur compounds. The damage doesn't stop at the mouth either — those bacteria can slip into the bloodstream and trouble the heart and kidneys down the line.

2. Kidney trouble (BUN running high) ⚠️

When the kidneys aren't filtering properly, blood urea nitrogen (BUN) climbs. Urea finds its way out through the breath and gives an ammonia or urine-like smell — vets call this "uremic breath." If your dog's breath smells like ammonia, get bloodwork done. Don't wait.

3. A high-protein diet 🥩

A 2022 study (PMC7472411) showed that high-protein diets shift the gut microbiome and grow protein-fermenting bacteria. Some of those metabolites end up in the breath. Red meats like lamb and kangaroo make the effect worse.

4. Digestion problems

Indigestion, food allergies, or a parasite load can all push gas back up into the mouth. Rotting food in the gut gives off a sour smell that travels.

A real case: Dim Sum's situation

Dim Sum is an 18kg dog. The pattern here is useful:

  • BUN on the high side (Sept 2025 bloodwork) — kidneys are working harder than they should.
  • Main food is lamb + kangaroo kibble — high-protein red meat, which adds metabolic load.
  • Bad breath plus smelly saliva — likely a mix of kidney-origin ammonia and high-protein diet output.

Plan: check the teeth for tartar buildup, redo BUN and CREA on bloodwork, and figure out which factor is the bigger contributor.

What actually helps

🪥 Brushing (the single most effective thing)

Daily brushing with a pet-specific toothpaste and brush cuts bad breath significantly in trials. Never use human toothpaste — the fluoride is toxic to dogs.

🥬 Diet changes

  • If BUN is high, move toward a lower-phosphorus, lower-protein kibble and trim the lamb or kangaroo share.
  • Stir in fresh chopped parsley — a natural breath freshener.
  • A half-teaspoon of cold-pressed coconut oil mixed into the food adds lauric acid, which has antibacterial action.
  • Keep the probiotic going (if you're already giving one) to balance the gut.
  • Add more water stations or a pet drinking fountain — extra hydration dilutes BUN.

🏥 Routine checks

If bad breath sticks around or gets worse fast, run a full blood panel (BUN, CREA) and a dental exam. Ammonia-scented breath in particular can be a kidney warning sign.

Hong Kong specifics

Humidity: Hong Kong's damp climate lets oral bacteria multiply faster. Wash water bowls and chew toys more often than you would in a dry climate.

Fresh food culture: lots of HK owners feed home-cooked meals, which is great — but watch the protein ratio. If your dog is on lamb and kangaroo like Dim Sum, mix in leaner proteins (turkey, rabbit) or push the vegetable share higher.

FAQ

Is a little doggy breath normal?

Mild food-breath after a meal is one thing. A persistent foul smell is not. If you can smell it across the room, something's off.

Can dental chews replace brushing?

They help (NIH PMC10981081 showed measurable improvement in halitosis scores) but they don't substitute for actual brushing. Think of chews as a top-up, not the main event.

My dog's breath smells like ammonia. Is that an emergency?

Get bloodwork this week. Ammonia-scented breath is a textbook uremic-breath signal. If your dog is also lethargic, off food, or vomiting, that's an emergency clinic, not a wait-and-see.

  2. Effects of dental chew on halitosis in dogs. NIH. PMC10981081. 2024.
  3. Varying Protein Levels Influence Metabolomics and Gut Microbiota in Dogs. NIH. PMC7472411.
  4. Chronic Kidney Disease & Renal Failure. BluePearl Veterinary Partners.
